findings.claim: The registry is a closed 11-kind class: adding a kind means editing the Zod file, EpochModulePackInput, a Map field, a snapshot and a restore line in registerPack, a registerX, a getX and the domain barrel, and the accepted-core-model kinds (thread runtime, resource ledger profile, instrument profiles, presence tables, tellProfile, CharacterBible, pools) would make it a god-registry.
findings.bites_when: At the first of the core-model steps that adds a kind (presence tables or CharacterBible at 06-ish): roughly 60 lines of near-identical boilerplate per kind in one 796-line class, and a kind added in the wrong place in registerPack's fixed order fails its own reference check (offices need characters first).
findings.disconfirm: Considered that 11 kinds with stage-then-commit is fine today; it is. The risk is the per-kind cost times the 7-10 kinds the core model needs, plus that the repo already has the right pattern (StateSliceKey via defineStateSlice) and does not use it here.
findings.recommendation: Replace the class body with a typed kind table: defineModuleKind<T>({ kind, schema, idOf, validate(ctx), dependsOn }) and a pack as Record<kindId, unknown[]>. One generic registerPack loops kinds in dependsOn order, uses one staged-commit/rollback, and one typed get<T>(kind, id). Keep spaces/waypoints special-cased as the spatial core. Domain keeps the generic engine; each core-model module ships its own kind definition file.
findings.ignore_cost: Every new core-model kind pays the full boilerplate and review cost, and the registry becomes the file every change conflicts in.
